diagram_math_checks.result: Exactly the three elements a,b,c appear. The two solid rising segments a–b and a–c encode a<b and a<c. Neither relation has an intermediate element because P contains only a,b,c and b,c are incomparable. There is no b–c segment, matching the Given poset.

The orange singleton {a} is an antichain by the local antichain definition. Neither b nor c can be added because each is comparable with a; hence it is inclusion-maximal as established in proof step 1.1.

The blue pair {b,c} consists of incomparable elements, so it is an antichain. The only three-element subset contains a<b, so no antichain is larger than two, exactly as step 1.2 and def-height-and-width-of-a-finite-poset assert. Thus {b,c} is maximum, and {a} is not maximum. The dashed horizontal blue guide is an annotation, not a cover relation.

Fresh standalone original-resolution preview shows three labeled vertices, both cover segments, the orange maximal-antichain label and blue maximum-antichain label, with no literal TikZ markup or overlapping diagram objects.
